question: Should exact proposal review and request-time proposal-version binding become the permanent core Skill Workshop approval contract?
rationale: The branch is technically coherent but adds a model-facing action and intentionally changes an existing pending-approval outcome, so tests cannot determine whether this is the desired long-term product contract.

options.title: Adopt and prove the contract
options.body: Keep the review action and version-bound decisions, then require live proof of both legacy and bound lifecycle paths before merge.

options.title: Land preview only
options.body: Keep exact proposal previews while deferring the compatibility-sensitive pending-approval binding to separate design work.

options.title: Decline the API expansion
options.body: Retain current inspect and summary approvals if no feature owner wants to own the additional permanent contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt and prove the contract
recommendation.body: Keep the review action and version-bound decisions, then require live proof of both legacy and bound lifecycle paths before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The introduction commit provides the strongest broad ownership signal for the current Skill Workshop API and lifecycle implementation.
